headline: Stocks Rebound as Oil Slides: S&P 500 Jumps 2.35% and Chip Stocks Surge – Ticker Velocity
text: Key takeaways Stocks rebounded on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. The S&P 500 rose 2.35% to 7,549.94, the Nasdaq Composite rose 2.74% to 25,253.14 and the Dow rose 1,104 points, or 2.15%, to 52,389.75, according to Reuters. Oil did much of the work. Brent crude fell 5.8% to $92.57 a barrel after President Trump said renewed strikes on Iran were unlikely if negotiations progressed, per the Associated Press. Chip stocks bounced hardest. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose about 6.9% after losing more than 12% the week before. The October CPI report is due Tuesday at 8:30 a.m. ET. We previewed it in October CPI Preview. Index Close Change S&P 500 7,549.94 +173.08 points, +2.35% Nasdaq Composite 25,253.14 +673.71 points, +2.74% Dow Jones Industrial Average 52,389.75 +1,104.02 points, +2.15% Closing levels are from Reuters and the Associated Press . Reuters said it was the S&P 500’s biggest daily percentage gain since April 8 and the Nasdaq’s biggest since July 30. The AP said the S&P 500 was still 3.4% below its all-time high from last month, and that the market “recovered most of its big loss” from the week before. Breadth was strong. Reuters reported that all 11 S&P 500 sectors rose, nine of them by more than 1%, led by industrials and consumer discretionary stocks, each up more than 3%. Another account of the session, from HDFC Sky , had energy slightly lower, so the sector count differs by source. Why stocks rallied Oil fell. Brent dropped 5.8% to $92.57, down from more than $112 at the start of the month, the AP reported. HDFC Sky put US crude (WTI) at $86.19, down 5.1%. The AP said Trump told CNN that resuming strikes on Iran is “highly unlikely” if the U.S. sees progress in negotiations. Cheaper fuel eases pressure on inflation, which matters ahead of Tuesday’s report. Free newsletter The Morning Brief The five market moves that matter, in your inbox before the opening bell. Free, every weekday. Unsubscribe in one click. The AI selloff looked overdone to some. Reuters reported that Morgan Stanley and UBS called the previous week’s rout in AI stocks excessive. The semiconductor index jumped about 6.9% to 10,033.93 after its biggest weekly drop since April 2025. Yields stayed high. The 10-year Treasury yield ended near 4.87%, per the AP, still below last month’s peak above 5.30%. Reuters said markets were pricing a Fed rate hike in December with odds above 80%, up from about 71% on Oct. 30. See December Fed Rate Hike Odds for how that works. Biggest movers AMD rose about 13%, and the AP said it recovered its 11% loss from the previous week in one day. Broadcom rose about 8.8% (Reuters), and Constellation Energy jumped 10.5% after beating earnings estimates (AP). CoreWeave rose 5.6% after falling 15.4% the week before (AP). Nvidia was the exception. It fell about 4.3% (AP) and closed at its lowest since April 7, according to Reuters. The AP linked the drop to a New York Times report about CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a business executive the paper said U.S. intelligence had determined was gathering information for China. Nvidia’s board is investigating and said it has “no reason to believe” national security or company secrets were compromised, the AP reported. China’s foreign ministry called the allegations “nothing but smears against China.” What to watch next October CPI, Tuesday at 8:30 a.m. ET. September inflation was 3.7% from a year earlier, with energy up 20.4%, per the BLS . Monday’s oil drop came after October’s prices were set, so it will not show up in this report. October PPI, Friday, Nov. 13 , per the BLS schedule . Oil and Iran headlines. The rally leaned on a drop in crude, which can reverse as quickly as it came. Our earlier coverage: Brent Crude Settles at $117.64 . One strong day does not erase the prior week’s drop. This is news coverage, not investment advice. Frequently asked questions How much did the S&P 500 rise on Nov. 9, 2026? It rose 2.35%, or 173.08 points, to close at 7,549.94, its biggest daily percentage gain since April 8, according to Reuters. Why did stocks go up on Monday? Oil prices fell about 5.8% after President Trump said renewed strikes on Iran were unlikely if talks progress, and technology stocks bounced after the prior week’s selloff. Reuters also noted that Morgan Stanley and UBS called the AI-stock rout overdone. Why did Nvidia fall while other chip stocks rose? Nvidia fell about 4.3% after a New York Times report about CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a business executive, according to the Associated Press. The company’s board is investigating. When is the October CPI report? Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
